clips.send: Arithmetic logic unit (ALU). The calculator of the CPU: adds, subtracts and compares, using circuits built from logic gates like your adder. An 8-bit adder is just 8 adder circuits chained together, passing carries along. The ALU also checks things like “is the result zero?” — that powers JUMP IF ZERO.

clips.send: Program counter (PC). Holds the address of the NEXT instruction. After every fetch it adds 1 — unless a JUMP changes it. A JUMP instruction simply writes a new address into the PC. That is how loops work! Starting a program equals setting the PC to its first address.

clips.send: Clock. A crystal that ticks billions of times per second. Every tick moves the CPU one step forward. 3 GHz equals 3 billion ticks every second. Our CPU uses 3 ticks per instruction (fetch, decode, execute). Real CPUs overlap the steps (pipelining) and run several cores at once.

clips.send: Inside the CPU. A CPU follows a list of instructions stored in memory — one tiny step at a time, billions of times a second. Instructions and data are both just numbers in memory. 105 means “ADD the number in cell 05”. The three-step loop — fetch, decode, execute — is called the instruction cycle. Click a part (PC, IR, ALU, ACC, memory, screen) to learn its job, then press Step.

clips.send: Control unit. The boss of the CPU: it fetches each instruction, decodes it and tells the other parts what to do. It holds two special registers: the program counter (PC) and the instruction register (IR). It sends control signals along wires called buses to memory and the ALU.
clips.text: Control unit. The boss of the CPU: it fetches each instruction, decodes it and tells the other parts what to do.. It holds two special registers: the program counter (PC) and the instruction register (IR).. It sends control signals along wires called buses to memory and the ALU.

clips.send: Memory (RAM). Numbered cells (addresses) holding both the program and its data. The CPU reads and writes them very fast. RAM forgets everything when the power goes off. Files are kept on storage (SSD or hard drive), which keeps data without power but is slower. Try it: change a green data cell and run the program again.

clips.send: Instruction register (IR). Holds the instruction being worked on right now, so the control unit can decode it. In this CPU the first digit is the operation (1 equals ADD, 2 equals SUB, 3 equals STORE, 5 equals LOAD, 6 equals JUMP, 7 equals JUMP IF ZERO, 900 equals OUT, 000 equals HALT). The last two digits are an address in memory.

clips.send: Accumulator (ACC). A register that holds the number the ALU is working on. LOAD puts a number in, ADD changes it, STORE copies it out. Registers are the fastest memory of all — right inside the CPU. A modern CPU has dozens of registers, each 64 bits wide.

clips.send: 程序计数器，P C。存放“下一条”指令的地址。每次取指后自动加1——除非遇到跳转指令改变它。跳转指令就是把一个新地址写进PC。循环就是这样实现的！启动程序 等于 把PC设为程序的第一个地址。

clips.send: 运算器，A L U。CPU里的“计算器”：做加法、减法和比较，它的电路就是由你搭过的那种逻辑门组成的。8位加法器就是把8个加法电路串起来，把进位一位一位传过去。运算器还会检查“结果是不是0”——“为零则跳转”就靠它。

clips.send: 控制器。CPU的“指挥官”：取出每条指令、进行译码，再命令其他部件去做。它有两个特殊的寄存器：程序计数器，P C，和指令寄存器，I R。它通过叫作“总线”的导线向内存和运算器发出控制信号。

clips.send: 输出。把结果送到外部世界——这里是小屏幕，现实中是显示器、扬声器或打印机。输入，处理，输出，再加上存储：这就是每台计算机的“输入、处理、输出”模型。键盘、摄像头、传感器是输入设备；屏幕、电动机是输出设备。

clips.send: CPU里面有什么。CPU按照存放在内存里的指令清单工作——每次只走很小的一步，但每秒能走几十亿步。指令和数据在内存里都只是数字。105的意思是“把05号格子里的数加进来”。取指、译码、执行这个三步循环叫作“指令周期”。点击一个部件（PC、IR、运算器、累加器、内存、屏幕）了解它的作用，然后按“单步”。

clips.send: 时钟。一块每秒“滴答”几十亿次的晶体，每一下都让CPU前进一步。3 GHz 等于 每秒30亿次滴答。我们这台CPU每条指令用3个时钟周期（取指、译码、执行）。真实的CPU会让各步重叠（流水线），并且多个核心同时工作。

clips.send: 累加器，A C C。存放运算器正在处理的数。“取数”把数放进来，“加”改变它，“存”把它复制出去。寄存器是速度最快的存储器——就在CPU内部。现代CPU有几十个寄存器，每个64位宽。

clips.send: 内存，R A M。带编号（地址）的格子，既存程序也存数据。CPU可以非常快地读写它们。断电后，内存里的内容全部消失。文件保存在外存（固态硬盘或机械硬盘）里，断电不丢失，但速度较慢。试一试：改一个绿色的数据格，再运行一遍程序。
